title: Getting started
subtitle: Your first steps in Swiss German
description: Discover how Swiss German sounds and learn the first words and expressions you'll need in everyday life.

expectations.title: Hear and recognise Swiss German sounds and pronunciation
Start communicating with your first words, greetings and everyday expressions

rules.title: Two forms of German
rules.theory: Swiss German and Standard German are closely related, but they are not the same. Swiss German refers to a group of regional dialects used mainly in everyday conversations.
rules.takeaway: Swiss German is not simply Standard German with a different accent. It has its own vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation.

rules.title: Speaking vs. writing
rules.theory: In Switzerland, people use Swiss German and Standard German in different situations.

points.heading: Everyday conversations
items: Swiss German is commonly spoken with friends, family and colleagues.
Spoken dialect is also common in many workplaces and social settings.

points.heading: Formal and written communication
items: Standard German is generally used in official documents, newspapers and formal writing.
Swiss German is also frequently written in informal messages, chats and social media.

rules.takeaway: Swiss German is not only spoken. You will also encounter it in written everyday communication.

rules.title: How is Swiss German written?
rules.theory: Unlike Standard German, Swiss German has no single official, standardised spelling system. People often write words in ways that reflect how they pronounce them.
rules.takeaway: There is no single correct spelling for every Swiss German word. Different writers may use different spellings.

rules.title: One word, different spellings
rules.theory: Swiss German spelling can vary between regions and individual writers. The same word may appear in different written forms.

points.heading: What this means
items: You may encounter different spellings for the same expression.
Regional dialects can also use different vocabulary and pronunciations.

rules.takeaway: Don't worry about memorising every spelling variation. Focus on recognising and understanding the words.

rules.title: Your learning convention
rules.theory: To make learning easier, Hoi uses one consistent spelling convention for each dialect.

points.heading: In Hoi
items: The same spelling is used throughout the lessons.
Words are written to reflect pronunciation as closely as possible.
Audio examples connect written words with their actual sounds.

rules.takeaway: You don't need to learn every spelling variation. Start with the convention used in your chosen dialect.

rules.title: Letters don't always sound the same
rules.theory: Swiss German uses the same Latin alphabet as English, but many letters and letter combinations are pronounced differently.

items.text: A distinctive sound that is uncommon in English.
A vowel sound that does not exist in most English accents.
A letter combination with its own characteristic sound.

rules.takeaway: Don't assume that Swiss German letters sound like English letters. Learning their sounds will help you read and pronounce new words.

rules.title: What you will learn next
rules.theory: Now that you understand the basics of Swiss German spelling, it's time to explore its pronunciation.

items.text: A, E, I, O, U and special vowels such as Ä, Ö and Ü.
Sounds such as CH, SCH and R.
Combinations such as EI, IE and AU.
How words and sentences flow naturally.

sections.description: Learn how to pronounce Swiss German sounds.
